items.text: Glad to secure a $35/month insulin cap for those on Medicare. But we must also work to prevent diabetes and make sure those with the disease have the other resources they need to manage it — glad to see suggestions that mirror my Prevent Diabetes Act. https://t.co/XYXXNTvuP3

In Virginia, 127,124 women and children are at risk of not receiving vital nutrition assistance during a government shutdown.

Shutdowns aren’t victimless crimes. The House should pass the bipartisan CR the Senate is working on.

In the Senate, we took a big step towards keeping the government running by passing a minibus.

It’s a targeted spending bill that supports military construction, nutrition programs, key veterans’ benefits, and important transit needs.

The House should pass it.

Let’s do a quick refresher on what a shutdown means:

Federal employees and servicemembers don’t get paid. 

Critical vets’ and nutrition assistance benefits lapse. 

Countless federal functions are derailed.

Let’s defuse this political hand grenade and pass a spending bill.

Fentanyl is killing more Americans than car accidents.

We need an all-of-the-above approach to address this crisis, from expanding telehealth addiction treatment to investing in better narcotics scanning tech at our ports of entry.

When Elmo checked in, folks weren’t doing so well. It’s why I’ve fought to invest in resources like 988 – the mental health crisis is real, and we need actual resources for folks in crisis. I’m going to keep fighting for resources for mental health.
https://t.co/V0KSrQo0Eh

Glad to spend the afternoon in Leesburg dropping off $4 million for a 24/7 Crisis & Stabilization Center. Funding comprehensive treatment for mental health issues is urgent and essential, and I was glad to hear perspectives from providers from across the region. https://t.co/HFYg1hJvvs

Folks suffering from substance use disorder need and deserve access to quality care. Thrilled to announce $650,000 for the Appalachian Center for HOPE’s new residential treatment center in Marion today, tour the future site, and hear more about their incredible work! https://t.co/nEXVy8BnZM

I was proud to secure $174,000 back in 2022 to better support the mental health of our law enforcement officers who do so much to keep Virginia communities safe. It’s crucial that we continue to break down barriers to mental health treatment in law enforcement. https://t.co/mIrl9ledrE

May is National Treatment Court Month. I’m proud to consistently advocate for more federal funding to support treatment courts, which help address the substance use disorder crisis, connect people with the resources they need, and reduce crime and recidivism.

Amid an extraordinarily challenging diagnosis, @RepWexton is serving Virginians with strength and tenacity. I’m proud our legislation to create a national plan to address Parkinson’s has passed the Senate and will be signed into law!

The fentanyl crisis has taken far too many too young. I support us taking wide-reaching action – from addressing fentanyl trafficking directly to expanding treatment options for those suffering from addiction – to save lives and end the crisis.

Deeply moved and incredibly inspired by the resiliency of @RepWexton. Amid a challenging diagnosis, her fierce advocacy for Virginians and those with disabilities persists. I’m thankful AI gave us the opportunity to hear her voice on the House floor again today. https://t.co/zhZxKk7ex3

Patients need consistent access to the telehealth flexibilities they have come to rely on. If the DEA can’t get a workable proposal done soon, it will be time for Congress to act to protect patients. https://t.co/pvsvndJAMr

It was great to be in Stuart to drop off $1.1 million for a backup power system for the local water treatment center. 

It’s easy to take clean water for granted — but the second it’s not available, it’s an emergency. Glad to get this project done for Patrick County! https://t.co/uA3LOmlWdg

We’re ticking closer to the expiration of telehealth flexibilities.

We can’t let people that rely on telehealth prescription for essential medications – including treatment for substance use disorder – have their access to care lapse. I’m pushing to renew flexibilities.

Last week, I was in Stuart to drop off $1.1 million for improvements to their water treatment system. It’s a great step for the community.

These types of projects are what’s at stake with passing real spending bills – we need to get them done to unlock more funding for Virginia. https://t.co/GVdrmu6XoH

Communities across the Commonwealth have faced threats to their critical infrastructure, including water treatment, since Helene. To stay safe, make sure to tune into guidance from your local officials over the next few weeks. https://t.co/QBemvTDisw

Access to contraception, abortion, and IVF is a fundamental part of health care. Any attempt to curtail that hurts women and endangers lives. I stand firmly with a woman’s right to access the treatment her doctor recommends.
Rep. Wexton served Virginians tirelessly and well, even through a terrible diagnosis. Her perseverance and legacy of service will not be forgotten. We are all stronger for knowing Jennifer.

Thrilled to see Virginia get $26 million in federal funding for wastewater treatment improvements in Lee County! Our disaster aid supplemental is going to build Southwest Virginia back stronger than it was before Helene hit.
Read more here: https://t.co/NoxH2Cv0kQ
Unbelievable. Hearing the Trump admin has cancelled tens of millions in funding for resiliency projects across VA, including funding to improve Richmond’s Water Treatment Facility.

Folks, extreme heat can be deadly, particularly for our elderly neighbors.

Check in on neighbors, stay hydrated, and seek medical attention immediately if you or a loved one is experiencing symptoms of heat stroke or heat exhaustion.

Ben, a disabled 14-year-old from Chesterfield, VA, isn’t “minutiae.” 

His health insurance isn’t minutiae. 

His future isn’t minutiae. 

Medicaid matters and I am fighting to protect it. https://t.co/UAZ75G9cdl
